A small wizened elderly man, a Bolivian weather spirit, standing at the entrance of a rocky cave while rain clouds pass overhead. Short human proportions, deeply lined face, simple modest earth-toned clothing. No wings or horns.

The Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui: an extremely tall, very thin dark-haired humanoid with unusually long arms and broad shoulders, emerging through Scottish mountain fog over gravel. Dark skin and dark body hair, no horns, no wolf face; distinguish the tall thin build from a bulky Bigfoot.

The specific 1792 kibyoshi variant of Amefurikozo: a small humanlike yokai with ONE eye centered on the face, wearing a wide woven bamboo hat and a simple modest Edo robe, standing in rain on a Japanese path. Depict this one-eyed bamboo-hat variant only; no paper lantern or umbrella merging from another variant.

A hairy man-sized ape with visibly long fingernails, four ape limbs and no tail, at a cave near the forested foot of Mount Kanlaon, Negros. Natural ape face and posture, rough dark fur. No horns, clothing, weapons, or human-wolf hybrid anatomy.

One enormous natural serpentine being moving beside the pale salt expanse of Lake Frome toward the red rocky Gammon Ranges in South Australia. One snake head, one continuous thick legless body, long tapering tail; no wings, legs, horns or invented sacred symbols. The immense scale and landscape tell the water-drinking-serpent story.

An uncanny elderly Japanese woman yokai in a modest worn robe at the sheltered entrance of an abandoned rural temple on a rainy evening, holding a shallow bowl of red beans as an editorial evocation of bean sounds. Human anatomy, aged face, eerie listening pose; no horns or extra appendages.

A large serpent-like lake monster with short legs, each roughly eighteen inches long relative to the enormous elongated trunk, crawling out onto the stony shore of Bear Lake, Utah-Idaho. Show four short legs as an artistic anatomical choice, one reptilian head and a long tapering tail. No wings, horse head, or ocean ship.

A single huge snake suspended in the cloud-filled heavens, representing Bobbi-Bobbi in Binbinga Dreamtime accounts. One natural snake head, smooth continuous legless coiling body and tapering tail, no dragon horns or feathers. Warm high clouds and a distant northern Australian landscape. No borrowed Aboriginal dot-painting motifs or invented ritual symbols.

The Boyg in its Norwegian giant slimy serpent variant: an immense glossy dark snake coiled across and completely obstructing a narrow rocky forest path. One snake head, continuous legless coils, no horns, wings or humanoid troll parts. Wet stones and northern conifers at dusk.

A strong short dwarf guardian on an Anglo-Scottish moor, wearing brown clothes, with red hair and very large bull-like eyes set in an otherwise human face. Stocky human body, heather and rocks; no bull head, horns or hoof feet. The brown attire, red hair and imposing eyes must read clearly.

Chernava, the Russian river maiden from Sadko: a human woman's head and upper body with ONE long fish tail instead of legs, beside a quiet river at dawn. Modest linen upper garment as an editorial treatment, unadorned natural face; long tail and broad fish fin fully visible. No wings or bird feet.

Cliodhna in the County Cork beauty-and-healing-birds tradition: a dignified adult woman in a flowing modest cloak beside coastal rocks, with EXACTLY THREE small songbirds visibly perched near her. One bird on a rock at her left and two spaced on a branch at her right. Birds not wings growing from her body; no crown required. Soft Atlantic light.

Irish Dullahan in the headless-rider variant: one fully clothed headless rider on ONE black horse, carrying his own ashen-pale head under one arm. The rider's raised collar ends in clean supernatural darkness, no wound or blood. Head has two fiery eyes. Whole horse with four legs visible on a misty Irish road; no pumpkin head or coach.

Each-uisge in its full horse variant: one powerful unbridled horse emerging from a deep Scottish Highland loch, dripping coat and wet mane, all four ordinary hooved legs visible in shallow water, alert unsettling gaze. No rider, fish tail, wings, horns, or hybrid human parts.

El Hombre Caiman of Plato, Colombia, in the explicitly recorded MAN'S HEAD / ALLIGATOR BODY variant: an adult man's head joining directly to a low crocodilian neck and four-legged alligator body with broad armored back and long reptile tail. No human chest, arms or extra crocodile head. On a muddy Colombian riverside, respectful non-comic painterly treatment.

Enenra, Japanese smoke yokai: a single loosely human-shaped figure made entirely of swirling dark gray smoke rising from a small rural hearth fire. Face, arms and body suggested by smoke rather than solid flesh. Soft luminous embers illuminate the transparent wisps. No horns, solid armor, demon wings or burning person.

The Fachan from Campbell's Scottish account: a giant with exactly ONE centered eye, exactly ONE muscular arm growing from the MIDDLE OF THE CHEST ending in one hand, exactly ONE leg below the torso, and ONE stiff tuft of hair. Shoulders have no additional arms. Front full-body view on a rocky Highland slope makes each unusual feature unmistakable. Modest ragged waist cloth. No extra limbs, weapon or horns.

Gallinipper tall-tale mosquito: one fantastically giant mosquito with exactly six long jointed legs, one pair of transparent wings, slim segmented abdomen and a long needlelike proboscis, beside tree trunks of comparable height in an American woodland. Mosquito anatomy, never a dragonfly, beetle or bird. No feeding or blood.

Gwyllgi, Welsh phantom mastiff variant: one massive BLACK MASTIFF with broad heavy head and clearly glowing red eyes, four canine legs, natural tail, standing on a lonely stone-walled Welsh road at twilight. The complete dog silhouette is visible; no wolf-werewolf body, horns or fire breath.

A wizened very old woman of European fairy-tale tradition, with a deeply lined angular face and gnarled hands, stooped beneath a rough modest shawl by an overgrown hedge. A tense enigmatic expression conveys the supernatural role. No pointed witch hat, broom, horns or oversized fantasy weapons.

Henwen, Old White of Welsh legend: one large WHITE SOW with a rounded pig body, bristly coat, long snout, four short cloven-hoofed legs and curled tail, crossing a lush Welsh field of young grain. Female domestic-pig form only; no boar tusks, wings or extra animals emerging from her body.

One Japanese hitodama in the documented bluish-white variant: a softly luminous ROUND ghostly fireball with ONE long curving tadpole-like flame tail, floating just outside the open doorway of an old Japanese wooden house at night. It has no face, eyes, human body or wings. Let the round core and trailing tapering tail read clearly.

A Yorkshire hob: a very small hairy wizened man with mischievous kindly face working quietly in an English farmhouse at night. Crouched beside a wooden grain bucket that establishes his small scale, modest simple worn clothes with hairy hands and feet visible. No elf wings or pointed hat. Warm hearth glow.

The North American hoop snake variant: ONE continuous snake grasping its OWN tail tip in its jaws to form a complete upright circular wheel, rolling along an open dusty track. Side-on view, unmistakable small snake head clamped around tail at the upper side of the circle. No extra snakes, broken disconnected coils, legs, wings or inner spines from the Australian variant.

Kipsy, Hudson River Monster: one immense elongated legless aquatic serpent with a small serpentine head and several continuous low back coils breaking the broad Hudson River surface. New York river bluffs and a tiny distant nineteenth-century sailboat establish location and scale. No horns, wings, plesiosaur flippers or Native American sacred motifs.

Humbaba as the Mesopotamian anthropomorphic Cedar Forest guardian: a formidable hairy ogre-like humanoid with a monstrous heavily ridged face and lionlike claws on his hands and feet. Two arms, two legs, upright full-body stance among tall cedar trunks, modest plain waist wrap. No lion head, extra heads, wings, modern armor or borrowed game design.

Ikuchi, Japanese sea-serpent yokai: an extraordinarily long legless serpent arching over a small Edo-period wooden fishing boat, leaving glossy dark viscous oil dripping from its belly onto the planks. One snake head and one continuous tapering body with far coils receding into deep sea. No arms, legs, horns or tentacles. No people in distress.

Jenglot of Indonesian folklore: a tiny eerie humanlike doll about twelve centimeters long, desiccated brown surface, exceptionally long dark hair and long fingernails, lying on a folded plain woven cloth. Macro still-life composition with a normal-sized leaf for scale. Modest cloth covering the torso and waist. No blood, gore, exposed organs or claim that it is a real living specimen.

One Okinawan kijimuna tree spirit, appearing as a small child with vivid red hair, perched in the branching roots of an enormous banyan tree. Modest simple woven tunic, ordinary human hands and feet, lively playful gaze. Red hair and banyan setting are the identifying features. No horns, pointed elf ears or wings.

Korbolko, the Turkic fire bird: one magnificent large bird with exactly two wings and two bird legs, majestic plumage blazing with red and golden-yellow light. Feather structure remains clear within the flame-like glow, especially a sweeping tail feather. Full bird above a dim orchard, no extra heads, human face, text or dragon anatomy.

A traditional mermaid: one adult woman with ordinary human head, arms and upper torso, transitioning at the waist into ONE long scaled fish tail with broad tail fin. Sitting side-on on a sea rock so the full tail is visible. Modest opaque woven wrap covers the chest; restrained natural sea-green scales, calm open ocean. No human legs, bird wings, trident or crown.

Mobile Wolf Woman, Alabama, in the documented WOMAN'S HEAD / WOLF BODY variant only: one wolf-bodied quadruped with four wolf legs, furry wolf torso and tail, and a human adult woman's head attached directly at the animal neck. No human torso, human arms, second wolf head or two-legged werewolf form. A quiet Mobile woodland edge at dusk.

Momo, the Missouri Monster: one large shaggy hairy humanoid resembling a bipedal ape, roughly seven feet tall, standing at the edge of rural Missouri woods. Two long arms and two legs, thick untidy brown fur, ape-like face partially framed by hair. Natural eerie evening light; no horns, alien costume, wings or extra limbs.

Moryana in the Volga-mouth WIND-SPIRIT variant: one stern exceptionally tall adult woman with uncombed windblown hair in a long modest WHITE garment, standing over Caspian coastal reeds as southeast winds bend them. Human anatomy and full body; no fish tail, mermaid accessories or blended fish transformation.

Nang Ta-khian: one adult Thai female tree spirit in a modest reddish-brown traditional Thai wrap dress, standing beside the huge buttressed trunk of a Hopea odorata tree. Gentle eerie forest light, natural human features, long dark hair. Tree trunk bears a simple colored satin wrap. No green dress, banana tree, horns or wings; do not confuse her with Nang Tani.

Nihang of Chitral: one enormous scaly WINGED SNAKE with a flowing GOLDEN MANE behind its reptilian head, rising over a mountain lake in the Mastuj landscape. One continuous serpentine trunk and tapering tail, two fully visible membranous wings, no legs or humanoid features. Golden mane and snake silhouette are unmistakable.

Nure-onna in the Edo illustrated snake-bodied variant: one adult WOMAN'S HEAD with long soaking-wet black hair joined directly to a long thick SNAKE BODY coiled beside a Japanese river. No human torso, arms, legs, baby, horns or second snake head. Keep her human face and wet hair clear, the continuous scaled body fully readable.

Penghou, the Chinese tree spirit, in the recorded black dog WITHOUT A TAIL variant: one entirely black natural dog standing next to the freshly split interior of an old tree trunk. Show a rear three-quarter side view so the smooth tailless rump is clearly visible, while its head turns toward the viewer. Four canine legs, no tail stump, horns or human face.

Pua Tu Tahi from Tahitian Rata mythology: one enormous monster CLAM on the deep ocean floor, two strongly ridged matching shell halves slightly open around a luminous fleshy mantle. Ordinary bivalve form magnified to colossal scale, nearby small fish establish scale. No human eyes, teeth, limbs, pearl or extra shell valves.

The generic Shadow Person variant, NOT Hat Man: a single near-black featureless upright human silhouette standing in the far end of a dim domestic corridor, edges subtly dissolving into shadow. Two arms and two legs, no visible face, eyes, hat or material clothing detail. Quiet uncanny low light rather than jump-scare.

A Philippine sirena water guardian: one adult woman with human head, two arms and torso, and ONE fish tail from the waist down, seated on a tidal rock beside a tropical Philippine coast, singing with gently parted lips. Long dark hair, modest opaque woven chest wrap, bronze-green scales, broad fish tail fin fully visible. No human legs, bird wings, European crown or trident.

Sundel Bolong in Indonesian folklore: one adult female ghost with very long black hair and a long white dress, seen from a rear three-quarter angle. Hair sweeps slightly aside to reveal the defining LARGE DARK SUPERNATURAL HOLLOW IN HER UPPER BACK, visible through an opening in the fabric. The hollow is a clean featureless shadow void, not a wound: no blood, exposed tissue, organs or gore. Face turns partly toward camera. Quiet rural Indonesian night path. Do not render as a plain Kuntilanak without the back hollow.

Surale in the Tatar forest-spirit variant: one humanlike creature with a WOOLLY BODY, exactly ONE HORN centered on the forehead, and unusually LONG THIN FINGERS on two clearly shown hands. Two legs, bent woodland pose, full body in a dense forest, modest rough waist cloth. No antlers, goat head, wings or human-peasant alternate form.

Tangie in its Scottish island full HORSE variant: one four-legged horse heavily draped in wet brown-green FUCUS SEAWEED, including flat branching fronds with small paired air bladders, standing at an Orkney or Shetland rocky shore. Horse muzzle, mane and four hooves remain identifiable. No fish tail, human head, wings or mermaid form.

Tenome, the Japanese yokai resembling a blind guildsman: one aged bald humanlike man in a modest Edo robe, with smooth EYELESS FACE and ONE clear eye centered in EACH PALM. Both hands held open toward the viewer, palms and their eyes fully visible, ordinary five fingers per hand, no eyes anywhere on the face. Full figure on a quiet Japanese graveyard path; no blood or injury.

Vegetable Lamb of Tartary: one small woolly lamb, four normal lamb legs and a sheep face, attached at the belly by ONE flexible plant stem to a living broad-leaved plant rooted in soil. It grazes the nearby grass within the stem's reach. Show both plant and lamb with the connecting stem unobscured. Botanical folklore illustration, no exposed anatomy, multiple lambs, tree-shaped legs or lettering.

A White Lady ghost: one sorrowful adult female apparition in a flowing modest white dress on a rural path near the distant Montmorency waterfall in Quebec. Nearly translucent edges, human face and hands, quiet grief rather than aggression, moonlit spray. No back hole, fangs, demon horns or other folklore-specific invented anatomy.

Wulver in Jessie Saxby's Shetland account: one benevolent MAN-BODIED figure with a WOLF HEAD, body covered in short brown hair, sitting upright on a rock beside deep water while holding a simple fishing line. Two humanlike arms and two legs; modest worn trousers, wolf muzzle and ears clearly visible. No transforming werewolf scene, full moon, bared fangs or aggression.

Yali of South Indian temple iconography, choosing the museum-described LION-FACED variant with ELEPHANT TRUNK: one lion-bodied quadruped with a lion face and mane, a long elephant trunk projecting from the muzzle and two ivory tusks. Four lion paws, natural lion tail, no human parts, wings or horse anatomy. Pose beside a weathered South Indian temple pillar; all defining anatomy clearly readable.
